claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks an adequate tutorial or guidance system to explain the mechanics, controls, and functions of available parts.

citations.review_text: ah yes, the "game" that leaves you with no tutorial on how to play. just throws you there and gives all the options available and let you try things out for yourself. mind you, there is a sandbox option. there is no fun in this, i am not watching ten thousand videos online just to understand the basics, because that's on you to make the process understandable and the game approachable. its one of those games that looks nice and all but it will disappoint because of how complex it is right from the start. like imagine, your first stage in game and you already have almost everything unlocked to use, it just kills it.
This game is really boring in my opinion it doesnt really teach you the mechanics of parts and I wish i didnt spend money on it.

I tried to give this game the college try but it doesn't make any sense and the tutorial is really poor.  It gives a bunch of things to do but most of them don't make any sense and there is no way to figure out what they do.  When it does give a tutorial, it doesn't explain what something does, how to use it, sometimes it doesn't even tell you what part of the screen to click on.  It's supposed to be a siege weapon game but none of the ranged attacks have multiple uses (at least in early game), and trying to move the siege weapon is not only hard to get it to go where you want, which it rarely even drives straight, the wheels fall off for no discernable reason and the machine gets stuck on any type of debris on the ground then you have to go back to the build menu and start over.
Tutorial seems insufficient for the game, it takes time to discover what every avaliable part does.

Cool to mess around with for a dollar and a half. Probably the worst "tutorial" I've ever seen in my life. Guess ill have to look elsewhere to get a grasp on the basics since the game doesn't want to explain itself in the slightest. 'Add a piston'. Okay. To where? For why? That's the extent of help it gives.

As a Linux user I can't recommend this game. 
In my hour of playtime I've had it crash multiple times, controls keep resetting to defaults, and tabbing out breaks the window completely for some reason... These issues seem to have been around for a long time (being especially bad on steam deck) - so I'd advise against buying it if you're on any Linux based software.

Gameplay wise I found the game to be incredibly unfriendly to beginners, having basically no form of guidance beyond "place this block once". The variety in mechanisms is really cool and I know you can build some amazing machines, but the sheer lack of any explanation makes it extremely unintuitive. 

[i] Overall I'd say this game was really cool back in the day, but aged like milk on a summer's day. [/i]

I'm so confused and baffled that after 10 years the devs couldn't make a more comprehensive experience. The game at first seems really fun and intuitive however, the fact there isin't more of a tutorial or a guide on how to build these machines feel confusing. I keep seeing reviews complaining on how the game became boring and I think that is because the game doesn't grab you early enough due to a lack guidance in how to play this game. You need to really have some experience in builders like this or else you'll be dumfounded like I was! I just wish the game ran you through some more levels with an actual tutorial.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Engineers leverage automation tools and logic gates to construct advanced contraptions.

claims.claim: Reviewers note the inclusion of logic gates and sensors, allowing players to automate contraptions and build complex setups.

citations.review_text:
8/10 I absolutely love this game. It's got some expected quirks for a slightly comical medieval siege game, but it's brilliant. 

The structural integrity system is a nice mechanical flavor over similar games. The rest of the mechanics are wonderful as well. A few 'magical' liberties are taken but it feels generally applicable to real world engineering which is great. There is some strange physics wobbling and glitching which can be expected, but it plays fairly intuitively. I can accurately apply basic flight principles to a plane or drone and expect some good results from my solution. It does feel a little arcade-like in a few ways, but mostly in good ways.

The graphics feel naturally nostalgic and almost toy-like. I love the visual effects as well, explosions feel like a good mix of realistic and silly.

Some automation and user control is occasionally lacking but it has enough to build for most use cases. I was able to successfully create a functional auto-stabilization gyro so I'd say it's quite satisfactory. An advanced multipart logic or math block of sorts that allows more complex logic, almost script-like, would be infinitely valuable as logic gates take up a lot of space on a contraption. Keybinding feels good, property tweaking isn't bad at all, and creating new mechanical tools out of existing ones is mostly intuitive (e.g. large powered hinges out of pistons and smaller unpowered hinges or longer pistons using pulleys and sliders.)

The little enemies and animals are adorable and silly, but they can be frustrating at times. Their pathfinding is very inconsistent, they often get stuck running into walls. I love the bouncing knights running at my siege machines, it's incredibly amusing.

The campaign is a short but very fun experience. It's great to have a use case for my vehicles as opposed to strictly open-world games. Water DLC seems a bit performance-intensive graphically and somewhat computationally compared to the other levels.

As far …

Speaking with a bias, it's an absolute banger. If you like playing with Legos, you'll enjoy it! ALSO, MOST IMPORTANT FOR FOLKS LIKE ME:
THIS GAME HAS LOGIC GATES AND SENSORS!!! That means EXACTLY what you think it does. Do a "no manual control" run. Build the machine to automate world domination. There is no price limit. Do some insane stuff. I will never work for lockhead but this game got me the closest to it.

You can trigger button presses with the sensors and use it to stabilize whatever you're working on, no classical PID control since everything is I/O but it's still the best game of it's kind i've ever seen. Any further and it would be a simulator!

It's a game that demands patience and plenty of thought ... [i]might leave Tiktok addicts bored[/i] ... some levels are rock hard [i](I'm looking at you "Ambush") [/i] but eventually solving a tough level and seeing the STEAM Achievement 'pop' is bloody joyous!

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED 8/10

One of my favourite Steam games, even if i absolutely suck at it and i have no clue how to do things, but experimenting is so so fun and trying to finish levels with crude machines that are way more overcomplicated than necessary and dont work half the time is honestly great, i also recomend the DLC even if they are even harder

citations.review_text: I love this game the creativity in the levels and how you can make builds as complex or simple as you can get away with. some levels you can beat with a flame thrower on a car or catapult or alot of bombs and the work shop shows what you can do if think about it. try anything and everything mabey somthing that looks like it shouldn't work ends up working or a masterfully crafted work of art works just like you planed it to

Very fun game, you can go absolutely HAM with builds if you're so inspired. I think the sandbox might even be Turing-complete if you're into that but I don't know enough about the specifics of computing to say for certain (although at this point I'd be surprised if it weren't tbh)
